title: sessions: Add Copy Pull Request URL action and dedicated PR menu group

- Moved **Open Pull Request** and **Copy Pull Request URL** into a new, dedicated `2_pullRequest` context-menu group so they're visually grouped together and separated from the other context menu groups.

Agents Window idea #12 requested an easy way to copy a session's pull request URL directly from the session list, without needing to open the PR pill / picker first. Grouping the two PR-related actions together also makes the context menu easier to scan.

title: sessions: Scope close chat shortcut to Sessions focus
body:
## Summary

- scope the Agents window close-chat shortcut to actual Sessions-part keyboard focus
- preserve the standard close behavior for editors, the Files placeholder, and other focused surfaces
- document the focus-scoped shortcut in the Sessions accessibility help
- add regression coverage for the registered keybinding expression

Fixes #329185

## Root cause

`sessions.chatCompositeBar.closeChat` intentionally has a higher keybinding weight than the session-level and editor-level `Ctrl/Cmd+W` commands. It previously won whenever the Agents window was active, the current peer chat was closable, and `editorAreaFocus` was false.

That negative focus check did not identify chat focus. The managed empty Files editor intentionally does not take focus when it opens. Clicking its blank content can therefore leave neither the editor area nor the Sessions part focused. Because `editorAreaFocus` was false, the high-priority close-chat binding still matched and closed the peer chat instead of allowing the standard close-editor binding to close Files.

## Fix

The close-chat binding now requires `SessionsFocusContext`, which is driven by the focus tracker on the central Sessions part. This makes ownership positive and explicit:

| Keyboard focus | `Ctrl/Cmd+W` owner |
| --- | --- |
| Session chat content, input, or chat tabs | Close the active closeable peer chat |
| File editor or empty Files editor | Standard editor close behavior |
| Files tree, sidebar, panel, or another surface | That surface or the normal fallback binding |

Ownership follows keyboard focus rather than whichever editor tab happens to be active. The per-tab close button is unchanged because it invokes the same action through `Menus.SessionChatTab`, independently of the keybinding `when` clause.

The existing Sessions accessibility help now also exposes the focus-scoped Close Chat command through `<keybinding:sessions.chatCompositeBar.closeChat>` so screen-reader users can discover the interaction.

## Regression coverage

The new test reads the actual registered macOS keybinding and evaluates its `when` expression for:

- focused Sessions chat
- focused editor
- blank Files placeholder / body focus (`sessionsFocus=false`, `editorAreaFocus=false`)
- non-Agents windows
- the non-closable main chat

The blank Files-placeholder case specifically fails under the previous `!editorAreaFocus` predicate.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsRename.test.ts --grep "close chat|accessibility help"`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsActions.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsActions.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.ts`
- `node build/checker/layersChecker.ts`

`npm run typecheck-client` and the type-check phase of `npm run valid-layers-check` are currently blocked in this checkout by unrelated Agent Host/Copilot SDK type mismatches (for example missing `managedApprovalRequired` and `githubMcpToolConfig` properties). The focused tests, lint, transpilation, and import-layer validation pass.

title: chat: restore completion relevance
body:
## Findings

The inline attachment reference implementation itself never disappeared. The regression came from `e746b009aa1` / #328944, which added multi-root Agent Host file completions and then applied the current typed token as `filterText` to **every** Agent Host completion.

Monaco ranks completion fuzzy scores before `sortText`, so that broad override had two side effects:

- Attached context still had the highest `sortText` priority, but Agent Host results received an exact fuzzy match against the typed `#` or `@` token and displaced attachments before `sortText` was considered.
- Slash commands all received the same exact score against the typed token. For `/pet`, `/vscode-pet` therefore lost its natural fuzzy advantage and the list fell back to Agent Host order, placing it below much weaker matches.

The current-token override is only needed for file and folder completions. Those results are deliberately ordered by the Agent Host across multiple workspace roots, so giving them a common score lets `sortText` preserve that deterministic host order.

## Fix

- Match attached context with the editor's configured fuzzy scorer, then use the current token as its Monaco `filterText` so it competes on equal terms with Agent Host results.
- Preserve fuzzy relevance between matching attachments through `sortText`, refresh suggestions as `#` and `@` queries change, and handle punctuation and interior cursor positions.
- Restrict the common current-token `filterText` override to `File` and `Folder` completion kinds.
- Keep the real filter text for slash commands, skills, chats, and other non-file completions so Monaco restores its normal relevance heuristic. `/vscode-pet` now ranks above the weaker `/pet` matches shown in the regression screenshots.
- Retain deterministic Agent Host ordering for multi-root file and folder completions.

## Validation

- All 52 chat input completion tests pass.
- Regression coverage verifies `/vscode-pet` keeps its actual filter text for a `/pet` query.
- Existing coverage verifies multi-root file results still share the current-token score and preserve host order.
- Changed files pass ESLint, repository hygiene hooks, and `git diff --check`.

title: chat-lib: remove recursive npm publish lifecycle script

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
### Description

Publishing `@vscode/chat-lib` invokes `npm publish` recursively because the package defines a `publish` lifecycle script whose command is also `npm publish`.

This caused the `0.60.0` release pipeline to fail after the package had already been successfully uploaded. Retrying the publish job then failed immediately because npm package versions are immutable.

### Reproduction steps

1. Run the `chat-lib` pipeline with `nextVersion: auto` for a release branch.
2. Let the public ESRP publish complete.
3. Let the Azure Artifacts publish task run `npm publish` from `extensions/copilot/chat-lib`.

### Expected behavior

The package is published once to the configured registry and the publish task succeeds.

### Actual behavior

After the outer `npm publish` uploads the package, npm runs the package lifecycle script:

```json
"publish": "npm publish"
```

That nested publish attempts to upload the same version again and fails:

```text
npm error code E403
npm error 403 Forbidden - The feed 'vscode' already contains file 'chat-lib-0.60.0.tgz' in package '@vscode/chat-lib 0.60.0'.
```

Failing build: https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=461606&view=logs&j=96402fc9-2a3b-5f5b-76a0-9d033b413348&t=9d9ceb20-337e-5950-afce-28e2465934ee

### Root cause

**Confirmed:** `publish` is an npm lifecycle hook. The `publish` script in `extensions/copilot/chat-lib/package.json` recursively launches `npm publish` after the outer publish uploads the package.

The issue became visible after microsoft/vscode-engineering#3500 made Azure Artifacts publishing the default whenever `publishPackage` is enabled. The first publish attempt uploaded `@vscode/chat-lib@0.60.0` to the Azure feed at 2026-08-05 14:21:58 UTC, but the nested invocation failed on the duplicate. The job retry encountered that already-published version again.

### Proposed fix

Remove the redundant `publish` script. Publishing is already driven by the pipeline and does not require a package lifecycle script.

title: Copilot Chat edit/apply_patch tool stalls in an indefinite "tools changed"-style loop; no longer limited to MCP calls, survives full VS Code restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
### Environment
- VS Code: 1.132.0 (macOS, arm64)
- Extension: GitHub.copilot-chat, version 0.41 (2026-03-25)
- MCP server involved in earlier occurrences: a remote MCP server (company internal connector to Jira in our environment)

### Summary
In long-running Copilot Chat sessions, the extension host repeatedly logs
`[CopilotCLI] Handling tools changed notification for <server>` in a tight
~500ms loop that never self-resolves. This correlates directly with
`edit`/`apply_patch` tool calls appearing to hang or get silently interrupted
mid-turn. **Update:** the same stall has now also been observed originating
from the plain edit/create file tool with **no MCP call involved at all**,
and in the latest occurrence it **persisted through a full VS Code restart**
— previously the one reliable mitigation. Terminal/command-line tool calls
continued to work normally while the edit tool was stuck, suggesting the
failure is scoped to the edit/apply-patch code path rather than the whole
extension host.

### Root cause (MCP-triggered variant, confirmed via logs)
Two cooperating issues:

1. **Route/gateway leak** — every chat turn creates a new route + gateway for
   the MCP server. Gateways are "disposed" (`Attempted to dispose unknown
   gateway` warning — already gone from the tracking map) but the underlying
   **route is never removed**. `active routes` only ever increases across a
   session (observed 1 → 2 → … → 52+).
2. **Fan-out amplification** — after any tool call to that server, Copilot
   re-fetches `tools/list`. If the server's response isn't byte-identical
   across calls, `McpGatewayService` fires `Gateway <id> servers changed`
   **once per accumulated leaked route/gateway** (23 simultaneous lines at
   the identical millisecond timestamp were observed), each broadcasting a
   `notifications/tools/list_changed` to its client session — one upstream
   event becomes N client notifications, each re-triggering a `tools/list`
   re-fetch, sustaining the cycle indefinitely (~500ms cadence in our case).

### New evidence: not MCP-exclusive, restart no longer reliable
In the most recent occurrence (2026-08-06):
- The loop/stall triggered via the plain edit/create file tool, with no MCP
  tool call in the turn at all.
- A full VS Code quit+reopen did **not** clear it (every prior MCP-triggered
  occurrence cleared immediately on restart).
- CLI/terminal-based tool calls kept working normally throughout.

This suggests either (a) a structurally similar leak exists independently in
the edit/apply-patch tool's own request/notification routing, or (b) the
MCP-originated leaked state isn't fully cleared by a normal restart in all
cases and resurfaces through the edit tool's path instead. Either way, please
don't treat "restart VS Code" as a confirmed fix when triaging — it is
inconsistent in our reports.

### Minimum repro (MCP-triggered variant)
1. Keep a single window open across many chat turns with an MCP server
   configured until routes have accumulated well beyond 1.
2. Make one successful tool call to that MCP server.
3. Within ~1s, `Handling tools changed notification for <server>` begins
   firing every ~500ms and does not stop (12 notifications by +1s, 62+ by
   +15s, sustained 35+ seconds and counting in testing). A fresh window with
   0 accumulated routes does not reproduce it from the same tool call.

### Impact
- Sustained extension-host load; `edit`/`apply_patch` calls hang or silently
  fail/restart mid-turn.
- Recurring across multiple unrelated workspaces/repos, with increasing
  frequency (now multiple times per day in long sessions).
- Previously the only reliable mitigation was a full VS Code restart; this is
  no longer consistently effective (see "New evidence" above).

### Suggested fix
- Ensure routes (not just gateways) are actually removed when a chat
  turn/gateway is disposed, so they don't accumulate unboundedly per session.
- De-duplicate/debounce `servers changed` → `tools/list_changed` broadcasts so
  one upstream change produces at most one client notification.
- Investigate whether the edit/apply-patch tool has its own, independent
  request/notification queue that can enter the same "never torn down, only
  grows" failure mode, since it now reproduces without any MCP server in the
  loop.

body:
## Summary

- verify Codex and Claude native optional-dependency packages after Azure node_modules restoration or installation
- cover product compile, cache-builder, quality, web, Alpine, and Copilot cache paths
- support explicit target platform and architecture arguments for cross-architecture cache builds

## Root cause

Build 461711 restored an Azure Pipelines `Cache@2` node_modules archive and skipped `npm ci`. The existing root-cache guard was wired into the separate GitHub Actions cache workflow, while #324255 protected Agent SDK scratch installs. As a result, the Azure product-build cache path never invoked the check.

The poisoned cache was subsequently invalidated by #329299. These changes prevent another incomplete cache from being consumed or saved.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 
- OS Version: 

Steps to Reproduce:

### Bug Description

`ping` to a local network host fails with `sendto: No route to host` when run from the VS Code integrated terminal, but works correctly from the built-in macOS Terminal.app. `sudo ping` works from VS Code's terminal. This issue is specific to macOS Tahoe (2026).

### Root Cause Analysis

On macOS Tahoe, `/sbin/ping` is **no longer a setuid binary** (`-r-xr-xr-x` instead of `-r-sr-xr-x`). It now relies on **non-privileged ICMP sockets** (`SOCK_DGRAM` with `IPPROTO_ICMP`), which require the calling process's entitlement chain to include `com.apple.security.network.client`.

VS Code's code signature currently includes these entitlements:

```
com.apple.security.automation.apple-events
com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit
com.apple.security.device.audio-input
com.apple.security.device.camera
```

**`com.apple.security.network.client` is missing.** This means child processes spawned by VS Code (e.g., the shell in the integrated terminal) cannot open non-privileged ICMP sockets.

Terminal.app, as a system application, has full network entitlements, so `ping` works without `sudo`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code on macOS Tahoe (2026)
2. Open the integrated terminal
3. Run: `ping <any-host-on-local-network>` (e.g., another device on the same subnet)
4. Observe: `sendto: No route to host`

### Expected Behavior

`ping` should work from the VS Code integrated terminal the same way it does from Terminal.app, without requiring `sudo`.

### Actual Behavior

```
➜ ping 192.168.1.100
PING 192.168.1.100 (192.168.1.100): 56 data bytes
ping: sendto: No route to host
ping: sendto: No route to host
Request timeout for icmp_seq 0
```

### Diagnostic Results

| Test | Terminal.app | VS Code Terminal |
|------|-------------|-----------------|
| `ping 127.0.0.1` (loopback) | ✅ Works | ✅ Works |
| `ping <LAN host>` | ✅ Works | ❌ `No route to host` |
| `sudo ping <LAN host>` | ✅ Works | ✅ Works |

**Routing is correct** (same in both terminals):
```
➜ route -n get 192.168.1.100
   route to: 192.168.1.100
destination: 192.168.1.100
  interface: en0
      flags: <UP,HOST,DONE,LLINFO,WASCLONED,IFSCOPE,IFREF>
```

**ARP resolves correctly** (target host is reachable at Layer 2).

**`ping` binary is NOT setuid on macOS Tahoe:**
```
➜ ls -la $(which ping)
-r-xr-xr-x  1 root  wheel  170256 23 Jul 07:57 /sbin/ping
```

**VS Code entitlements (missing network.client):**
```
➜ codesign -d --entitlements - /Applications/Visual\ Studio\ Code.app
Executable=/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/MacOS/Code
[Dict]
    [Key] com.apple.security.automation.apple-events
    [Value] [Bool] true
    [Key] com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit
    [Value] [Bool] true
    [Key] com.apple.security.device.audio-input
    [Value] [Bool] true
    [Key] com.apple.security.device.camera
    [Value] [Bool] true
```

### What was ruled out

- ❌ **macOS Firewall** — disabled entirely, issue persists
- ❌ **Local Network permission** — VS Code is toggled ON in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network
- ❌ **Quarantine attribute** — could not remove due to SIP, but irrelevant since `sudo ping` works
- ❌ **Launching VS Code from Terminal.app** — does not change behavior
- ❌ **Routing / ARP** — both resolve correctly, same as Terminal.app

### Proposed Fix

Add `com.apple.security.network.client` to VS Code's entitlements plist:

```xml
<key>com.apple.security.network.client</key>
<true/>
```

This would allow child processes (including the integrated terminal shell) to open non-privileged ICMP sockets, restoring `ping` functionality without `sudo`.

### Environment

- **OS**: macOS Tahoe (2026)
- **VS Code**: Latest stable (downloaded from code.visualstudio.com)
- **Shell**: zsh
- **Architecture**: Apple Silicon (arm64)

title: agentHost: show multi-root sessions in empty and single-folder Editor windows
body:
## Problem

In the **Editor window** (not the Agents window), a Copilot Agent Host session created in a **multi-root workspace** would not appear in the agent-session list when:

1. **An empty (no folder) Editor window is open** — the multi-root session does not show up, even though empty windows are meant to show all sessions.
2. **One of the constituent folders is opened** (e.g. just `copilot-sdk` or just `copilot-agent-runtime`) — the session does not show up.

The Agents window was unaffected because it does not apply this workspace filter.

## Root cause

`AgentHostSessionListStore._isSessionInWorkspace` treated the `_meta.multiRoot.workspaceFile` branch as an **exclusive early return**, matching strictly by `.code-workspace` identity against `workspace.configuration`:

```ts
if (multiRoot) {
    return URI.isUri(workspace.configuration)
        && extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqual(URI.parse(multiRoot.workspaceFile), workspace.configuration);
}
```

`workspace.configuration` is a URI **only** in a multi-root (`WORKSPACE`) window — it is `null` in both empty (`EMPTY`) and single-folder (`FOLDER`) windows. So for a multi-root session this branch always returned `false` in those windows and never fell through to the empty-window "show all" rule or the working-directory containment check.

## Fix

title: Make agent-host tool search model allowlist configurable (or auto-trim tools for BYOK models like DeepSeek)
body:
## Summary

The agent host's **tool search (deferred tool loading)** feature is gated behind a hardcoded model allowlist (`agentHostModelSupportsToolSearch`). BYOK / third-party models (e.g. DeepSeek V4 registered via the `vizards.deepseek-v4-for-copilot` extension) are not in that allowlist, so agent-host sessions send **every enabled tool definition** to the model in a single request. Models with a per-request function-count limit (DeepSeek caps at 128) then fail with `502`.

## Problem

When using a BYOK model (e.g. DeepSeek V4 Flash) in a **Copilot agent host** session with many tools enabled (>128, commonly caused by MCP servers), the request fails:

```
Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times
Last error: 502 DeepSeek 单次 tools 请求最多支持 128 个 functions，当前请求包含 203 个。
```

### Root cause

In `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/toolSearchDeferral.ts`, `agentHostModelSupportsToolSearch(modelId)` is a hardcoded allowlist that only matches:

- GPT-5.4 / 5.5 / 5.6 variants
- Claude families 4.5 and newer

The launcher gates tool search on it (`copilotSessionLauncher.ts`):

```ts
const toolSearchActive = this._configurationService.getRootValue(copilotCliConfigSchema, CopilotCliConfigKey.ToolSearchEnabled) === true
    && agentHostModelSupportsToolSearch(effectiveModel?.id)
    && clientToolNames.has(CLIENT_TOOL_SEARCH_REFERENCE_NAME);
```

When the model is not in the allowlist, MCP and non-core tools are **not deferred**, and the SDK sends all tools up front — exceeding third-party API limits.

## Suggested changes (any one)

1. **Make the allowlist configurable** — e.g. extend `chat.agentHost.modelCapabilityOverrides` to accept a `toolSearch: boolean` capability field, or add a new setting like `chat.agentHost.toolSearch.models: string[]` (allowlist of model id prefixes) / `chat.agentHost.toolSearch.defaultForByok: boolean`.
2. **Default-enable tool search for BYOK models** — BYOK providers register through the LM API and typically support function calling (OpenAI-compatible), which is all the runtime `tool_search_tool` requires. Since BYOK is already an explicit opt-in (`chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`), defaulting tool search on for them is low risk.
3. **Advertise a per-model tool-count limit** through the BYOK bridge (`IByokLmModelInfo`) and have the SDK trim/group tools to fit it.

## Current workaround (verified NOT viable for BYOK)

Family aliasing is **insufficient** for BYOK models. Verified with agent-host logs:

```
Model capability override: routing prompt for 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash' as family 'claude-sonnet-4-6'
... still 502 DeepSeek 单次 tools 请求最多支持 128 个 functions，当前请求包含 204 个
```

The alias only affects VS Code's local capability layer. The **wire model id is unaffected** (`deepseek-v4-flash`), and the (closed-source) Copilot SDK runtime decides whether to honor `defer` based on that wire id — DeepSeek is not in its tool-search support set, so it ignores `defer: 'auto'` and forwards every tool. Both aliases below were tried; the 502 persisted.

```json
{
  "chat.modelCapabilityOverrides": {
    "deepseek-v4-flash": { "family": "claude-sonnet-4-6" }
  },
  "chat.agentHost.modelCapabilityOverrides": {
    "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash": { "family": "claude-sonnet-4-6" }
  }
}
```

Side effects (avoidable): the aliased family routes the system prompt and every Claude-family heuristic (multi-replace tools, context editing, PDF support, …) to a model that is not Claude.

**The real fix must live in VS Code / the agent host** (see Suggested changes above). The most promising option is #3 — have the BYOK bridge advertise a per-model tool-count limit (`IByokLmModelInfo`) and let the SDK trim/group tools to fit it — because it requires no model-specific allowlists and works for any BYOK provider.

## References

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/agentIntent.ts` — `allowTools[CUSTOM_TOOL_SEARCH_NAME] = !!model.supportsToolSearch`
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/chatEndpoint.ts` — `this.family = getModelCapabilityOverride(...)?.family ?? ...`
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/common/chatModelCapabilities.ts` — `modelSupportsToolSearch`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/toolSearchDeferral.ts` — `agentHostModelSupportsToolSearch` (hardcoded allowlist)
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts` — tool-search gating in `_buildSessionConfig`

## Environment

- VS Code: latest stable (Insiders also affected)
- Extension: `Vizards.deepseek-v4-for-copilot` (BYOK, vendor `deepseek`, models `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro`)
- Settings: `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled: true`
- Related source:
  - `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/toolSearchDeferral.ts`
  - `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts` (`_buildSessionConfig`)
  - `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/copilotCliConfig.ts` (`chat.agentHost.modelCapabilityOverrides`)

## Repro

1. Install a BYOK extension that registers DeepSeek (or any model whose API limits functions per request).
2. Enable enough tools (>128, e.g. via MCP servers) so the agent host forwards more than the model's function limit.
3. Start an agent host session with the BYOK model and send a request.
4. Observe `502 ... tools ... limit` from the model provider after 5 retries.

title: agentHost: Claude per-session provider selection
body:
Closes #329656

### What

Lets each **Claude** agent-host session pick a model whose **provider** decides its transport, instead of the whole host being pinned to one transport:

- `anthropic`-provider models route to the **native Anthropic SDK**.
- `copilot` (and any unknown) provider routes to the **Copilot-CAPI proxy**.

This mirrors how the Codex provider already behaves, and is always-on (no experimental flag).

### How

- **Provider-qualified model ids** — a small codec (`claudeModelSelection.ts`) encodes/decodes `@provider=anthropic:…` / `@provider=copilot:…`. Bare/legacy ids (no explicit provider) resume on the host default transport, so already-persisted sessions need no migration.
- **Merged catalog** — the model list is fetched from both the native and proxy sources, each self-gated on its own credential/native-setup, and re-stamped with `provider: 'anthropic' | 'copilot'`. The picker groups the rows by vendor ("Anthropic" / "Copilot").
- **Per-session transport resolution** — `resolveClaudeSessionTransport({ model, defaultMode })` maps the selected model's provider to a transport at materialize time.
- **Live switching** — selecting a model on the *other* transport defers via a pending-switch flag and re-materializes the session's subprocess on the next send, so the rebuilt process is routed to the newly-selected provider. Same-transport model changes still hot-swap in place.

### Notes / intended behavioral consequences

- **Merged/qualified catalog is now the default.** A Copilot-only user sees a single "Copilot" group; a dual-credential user sees both. Routing is unchanged (vendor stays `agent-host-claude`).
- **Copilot sign-in becomes lazy** — the Copilot resource is advertised `required: false`; sign-in defers to first send of a Copilot-routed model (matches Codex).

### Testing

- Unit: `claudeModelSelection.test.ts`, `claudeAgent.test.ts` (codec, merged-catalog refresh, per-session transport resolution, live cross-transport switch, signed-out native bootstrap).
- Agent-host e2e suite (`test/node/e2e/`) with `modelProviders: ['copilot', 'anthropic']`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`.
- Live smoke against a dual-credential build (picker grouping + lazy Copilot sign-in + native↔Copilot switch).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code with a file that has enough content to show the vertical scrollbar.
2. Move the mouse pointer to the far right edge of the screen.
3. Try to grab and drag the scrollbar thumb without precisely targeting it.
4. Notice that the rightmost edge area no longer activates the scrollbar.

### Expected

The scrollbar should remain draggable when the pointer is placed at the extreme right edge of the window, preserving the long-standing desktop interaction pattern where users can "throw" the pointer to the screen edge.

### Actual

The Modern UI rounded corner / increased spacing design leaves a gap between the screen edge and the scrollbar. The rightmost pixels no longer map to the scrollbar hit area, requiring users to precisely aim at the scrollbar thumb.

This is a usability regression caused by the Modern UI redesign.

### Reference

Microsoft Edge maintains compatibility with this interaction pattern by keeping the rightmost edge pixels mapped to the scrollbar hit area even with rounded window corners.

### Suggested fix

Keep the visual spacing and rounded corner design, but add an invisible edge hit area (for example, the outermost 1–2 px adjusted for DPI scaling) that maps to scrollbar interaction.

### Type of Bug

Regression

### Reproduction

1. Run a current VS Code Insiders build with the modern UI/style override and motion enabled.
2. Open Source Control.
3. Open a toolbar **More Actions...** menu for a repository.
4. Open **Branch** and invoke **Create Branch From...**.
5. Observe the quick pick.

### Expected Behavior

The command's quick pick remains open and focused.

### Actual Behavior

The Command Center/quick-pick surface briefly opens, then immediately closes and focus returns to the toolbar menu.

### Regression Details

The regression was introduced by c5f02db50896ef310d3c909628e651675644fcef ("Add open/close motion to button menus in workbench chrome", #325190).

Animated context views delay disposal for the close animation. During that interval, the closing toolbar menu remains focusable. title: Fix stale session changes document lifecycle
body:
## Problem

Switching away from or archiving an Agents-window session did not fully release the documents resolved by its **Changes** multi-diff editor. Files from an archived session worktree therefore remained live `TextModel`/`TextDocument` instances after the worktree was removed.

The TypeScript extension correctly mirrored those documents from `workspace.textDocuments`. Every replacement tsserver consequently reopened the stale TypeScript file and rebuilt a small project for the deleted worktree, recreating file watchers after session switches and watcher resets.

Persisted editor history, recently closed entries, view state, working-set serialization, and URI strings were investigated but were not the live document owners.

## Why the outer editor input remains alive

An editor pane and an editor input have different lifetimes:

- `SessionChangesEditor` is the reusable UI pane. When the workbench activates another editor, it calls `clearInput()` on the pane before assigning the next input. Clearing means “stop displaying this input and free pane-owned resources”; it does **not** mean that the corresponding tab/input was closed.
- `SessionChangesEditorInput` is the editor/tab identity. The editor group disposes an input only when that input is actually closed and is no longer open in any editor group. An input that was merely backgrounded or detached from the current pane therefore remains undisposed.

In the captured heap, the stale `SessionChangesEditorInput` had not crossed that close/dispose boundary (`_isDisposed` was false). `IEditorService.lastActiveEditor` still referenced it after the pane was cleared. That field explains why the undisposed object remained reachable; it does not prevent or veto disposal.

Session editor working sets add another important constraint. They preserve serializable editor identity so the Changes tab can be recreated when returning to a session. Deleting an archived session’s working-set entry removes that stored snapshot, but it is not an ownership API for any already-live `EditorInput`. Disposing the outer input from `clearInput()` would also be incorrect because `clearInput()` is used for ordinary input switches where the tab is still open and expected to work when selected again.

The required ownership split is therefore:

- Keep the cheap outer `SessionChangesEditorInput` alive for editor identity, matching, serialization, and restoration.
- Release the expensive resolved inner `MultiDiffEditorInput` whenever the pane clears, because it owns the text-model references.
- Lazily create a fresh inner input if the outer tab becomes active again.

## Root cause

`SessionChangesEditor.clearInput()` detached the multi-diff widget but did not dispose the cached inner `MultiDiffEditorInput`, which owned the `ITextModelService.createModelReference()` references for every diff resource. The outer input could legitimately outlive the visible pane, so those references inherited an unnecessarily long lifetime.

There was also a teardown race in the underlying multi-diff input: if the input was disposed while asynchronous model resolution was pending, the completed model and view model could later be registered into an already-disposed store and leak their text-model references.

Separately, tsserver event delivery was guarded only by server generation. A queued watcher-creation event could still be accepted after client disposal or a terminal server exit when no newer generation had started.

## Fix

- Own the lazily created inner `MultiDiffEditorInput` with a `MutableDisposable`.
- On `SessionChangesEditor.clearInput()`, first save view state and detach the widget, then release the resolved inner input and its document references.
- Keep the outer `SessionChangesEditorInput` alive; reopening it lazily creates a fresh inner input.
- Resolve multi-diff models into a temporary disposable store and transfer ownership only while the input is still alive. Late results are disposed deterministically.
- Dispatch tsserver events only while both the spawning generation and exact running server handle remain current.

## Validation

- Added focused coverage for releasing and re-resolving session Changes inputs while preserving the outer restorable input.
- Added pane-boundary coverage proving `clearInput()` releases resolved ownership.
- Added coverage for disposing text-model references that finish resolving after input disposal.
- Added coverage for stale-generation and inactive-server event rejection.
- Passed focused unit tests, TypeScript extension compilation, client type checking, layer validation, and Code OSS CI.

(Written by Copilot)

Fix https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8734

Summary
Copilot Chat appears to read and act on local `.claude` skill files even when no skill has been explicitly invoked for the current task. In this case, a read-only investigation request was treated as if it should follow an issue-refinement workflow, which is over-fit behaviour and not an acceptable default.

Problem statement
When the user asked to investigate an issue, the agent reached for a refine-issue style workflow from `.claude` rather than staying in investigative mode. This suggests that local skill instructions are being treated as active policy even when they are not part of the current task context.

Why this matters
- It breaks the boundary between plain investigation and workflow execution
- It can trigger unintended side effects, including issue mutations
- It makes agent behaviour harder to predict and trust
- It over-fits to local repo instruction files instead of following the explicit request

Expected behavior
- Skill files should only be used when a skill is explicitly invoked, or when the user clearly and directly asks for that capability
- Issue-related wording alone should not cause an issue-management skill to activate
- Read-only investigative requests should remain read-only
- Skills should not be treated as ambient policy just because they exist in `.claude`

Actual behavior
- The agent followed a refine-issue style path during an investigation request
- The presence of issue/status wording appears to have triggered skill selection
- The agent behaviour over-fitted to local skill instructions instead of the user's intent

Concrete example
User request:
Investigate why an issue is reported as In Progress and determine the code status.

Observed behaviour:
The agent reached for a refine-issue workflow path from `.claude`, even though no skill had been invoked.

Acceptance criteria
- Skills are only activated when explicitly requested by the user
- A plain investigative request does not invoke issue-management or refinement skills
- Presence of issue URLs, status text, or workflow labels does not by itself activate a skill
- The agent can still use skills when the user explicitly asks for them
- The behavior is reproducible and documented with a minimal prompt example

Environment

<!-- Searched existing issues; no matching report found. -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0 (built-in)
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 10.0.26200 (build 26200)
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: DeepSeek V4 Flash, provided by a third-party LanguageModelChatProvider extension (vizards.deepseek-v4-for-copilot 0.6.2)
- Logs: Sanitized request-dump summary below. I did not attach the full dump because it contains local conversation content.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a third-party language model provider and select its model in VS Code Agent mode.
2. Open a new Agent chat session.
3. In the tool picker, enable the `read` toolset and `readFile`. In persisted VS Code state, both `read=true` and `copilot_readFile=true`.
4. Reference the `#read` toolset in the prompt and ask the agent to read the first line of `README.md`.
5. Inspect the `options.tools` received by the extension's `provideLanguageModelChatResponse` implementation.

## Expected

The explicitly referenced toolset should be expanded before the request reaches the language model provider. `options.tools` should contain `readFile` (internally `copilot_readFile` / `read_file`), or contain an `activate_*` virtual tool that can expose it.

## Actual

The first observable provider input contains only these three tools:

```text
insert_edit_into_file
replace_string_in_file
session_store_sql
```

There is no `readFile`, `read_file`, `copilot_readFile`, or any `activate_*` tool.

The final API wire request contains exactly the same three tools. The provider extension dumps `options.tools` before its own tool-processing code runs, so the read tool is already absent at the VS Code/Copilot Host -> LanguageModelChatProvider boundary.

## Additional observations

- VS Code persisted tool state contains 105 enabled individual tools; the `read` toolset and `copilot_readFile` are enabled.
- The chat-session data parses `#read` as a toolset containing `copilot_readFile`.
- The behavior is consistent for the initial Agent turn. In another session, the initial turn received only the same three tools, while a later user turn received about 19 read/search tools including `read_file`.
- This also reproduced before installing a separate skills/hooks plugin, so that plugin does not appear causal.
- The third-party provider extension only converts the received tool schemas; it does not filter ordinary tools.

This looks like an interaction between per-turn/virtual tool selection and explicit toolset expansion for extension-provided language models.

body:
I don't think I understand the change in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/318985, seems that we now aggressively leak terminals.

---

## Type of Issue

Bug

## Reproduction

1. Open the Agent Window.
2. Activate several workspace-backed agent sessions. Each activation creates an Agent Host terminal for that session.
3. Mark those sessions as Done so their worktrees are removed.
4. Inspect the Agent Host process tree and open PTYs.

## Actual behavior

The terminal is moved to the background when its session is archived, but the Agent Host PTY and its interactive shell remain alive indefinitely. The worktree may be deleted while the shell still has it as its working directory.

In one live Insiders process after approximately 11 hours:

- 70 direct `/bin/zsh -il` children
- 70 `/dev/ptmx` handles retained by the Agent Host
- all 70 shells idle with no child processes
- 55 shells rooted in worktree paths
- 25 shells whose working directories had already been deleted
- about 32 MB aggregate shell RSS

Agent Host logs showed 71 terminal creations and only one terminal exit/disposal. Shell start times matched the `[TerminalManager] Creating terminal` log entries exactly.

## Cause

`SessionsTerminalContribution._onActiveSessionChanged` eagerly ensures a terminal whenever the active session changes. Its archive path calls `_hideTerminalsForSession`, which uses `moveToBackground` rather than disposing the terminal. This retention behavior is explicitly covered by the test `hides (does not dispose) terminals when session is archived`.

That policy conflicts with archive cleanup removing the session worktree, leaving a hidden interactive shell and PTY for every archived session.

Relevant history:

- [#297330](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/297330) introduced ensuring a terminal for every active session.
- [#318985](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/318985) intentionally changed archive cleanup from killing terminals to retaining them. This is the change most directly responsible for the retained shells.
- [#321506](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321506) moved the current lifecycle to session-ID ownership.

## Expected behavior

Archived sessions should not accumulate live Agent Host shells after their worktrees are removed. Possible fixes include disposing terminals when archive removes the owned worktree, or creating session terminals lazily only when the terminal surface is used.

(Written by Copilot)

Steps to Reproduce:

2. Switch the mode pill to **Editing** mode
3. Copy plain text from another editor
4. Place the caret in a paragraph and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>

Expected: the clipboard content is inserted at the caret.

Actual: nothing happens. Cut (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>X</kbd>) is also a no-op. No error is logged in the Developer Tools console.

Scope of the problem:

What works in Editing mode:
- Typing
- Deleting a selection with Delete / Backspace
- Copy (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and context menu)

What does not work in Editing mode:
- Paste (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>, <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>, and context menu "Paste")
- Cut (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>X</kbd> and context menu "Cut")

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Describe the feature you'd like

Custom agents (`.agent.md`) appear in the chat agent picker as plain-text entries without any icon, while built-in agents (Agent, Ask, Plan) each show a distinctive codicon. There is currently no way to assign an icon to a custom agent. I would like to declare one in the YAML frontmatter, e.g.:

```yaml
---
name: Design-temp
description: A specialized UI/UX design agent
icon: paintcan   # any codicon id
tools: [...]
---
```

## Describe the problem / motivation

- Users maintaining several custom agents (user-level + workspace-level) get a long, text-only list in the picker that is hard to scan. Icons would make agents visually distinguishable and faster to find, consistent with the built-in entries.
- The frontmatter already supports rich metadata (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`, `argument-hint`, `handoffs`, `hooks`, ...), yet the visual presentation is the only aspect that cannot be customized.

## Current behavior (verified against `main` sources)

- `PromptHeaderAttributes` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/promptFileParser.ts` has no `icon` attribute, so an `icon:` key in the frontmatter is silently ignored.
- `CustomChatMode.icon` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatModes.ts` is hard-coded to `constObservable(undefined)`.
- In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/modePickerActionItem.ts`, an icon is only resolved for modes where `isModeConsideredBuiltIn()` returns true (`builtinDefaultIcon` maps `ask` → `Codicon.ask`, `plan` → `Codicon.tasklist`); user/workspace custom agents always render without an icon. The file even contains the comment `// TODO: there should be an icon contributed for built-in modes`, acknowledging this gap.

## Describe the solution you'd like

1. Add an optional `icon` attribute to the `.agent.md` frontmatter (and to `PromptHeaderAttributes`), accepting a codicon id (e.g. `robot`, `paintcan`, `symbol-color`), consistent with how `ThemeIcon`/codicons are used elsewhere in VS Code.

title: tunnels: resume auto-reconnect on desktop and drop dead connections
body:
Tunnel-backed agent host connections could drop overnight and never come back, forcing a full manual re-run of the connect workflow (connect command → select tunnel → select workspace).

### Auto-reconnect paused permanently on desktop

After `RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` consecutive failures, `_pauseReconnect` cancels the retry timer and relies on something later calling `_resumeReconnects`. Its only triggers were an `online` event and `visibilitychange`, both registered behind `if (isWeb)`. On desktop the sole remaining caller was an added GitHub auth session.

The pause is terminal rather than merely delayed: `_reconnectPaused` isn't consulted as a hard gate, so it works by cancelling the timer and relying on nothing re-arming it. The re-arm normally comes from `_handleConnectionChanges` on an explicit Connected → Disconnected transition — but once paused you're already disconnected, so that transition never fires again. No timer, no transition, no resume trigger.

This routes `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus` into `_resumeReconnects` so both web and desktop recover on the next window focus, and drops the web-only visibility listener it subsumes. `_resumeReconnects` is still rate-limited by `RESUME_RATE_LIMIT_MS`, so focus churn can't hammer the relay.

A status check that confirms the host is online now resumes any paused address rather than only those parked with reason `hostOffline`, which makes `_hostOfflinePaused` redundant. The pause log message claimed recovery triggers that didn't exist on desktop; it now reports the real ones.

### Tunnel providers kept advertising dead connections

Only the SSH/configured-host contribution called `clearConnection()`, so a tunnel provider kept `_connection` pointing at a dead protocol client and went on advertising its sessions as openable. Opening one subscribed over the dead client, threw, and permanently poisoned that editor with "Couldn't open session" — the error is baked into the chat history at hydration time and never re-hydrates.

`_wireConnections` must run before `_handleConnectionChanges` for this, since it reads the previous status to detect the transition. The ordering is commented and covered by a test that fails if it's reverted.

### Notes

`clearConnection()` deliberately preserves the cached session list, so offline sessions stay visible; this is not `unpublishCachedSessions()`.

Already-open editors still can't self-heal after a reconnect — the stale `ChatModel` is retained by `ChatService._sessionModels` and `ChatEditorInput.modelRef`, so refreshing them needs `ChatService.loadRemoteSession` to make its contributed-session bindings replaceable. That's shared chat machinery and out of scope here; this PR reduces how often tabs get poisoned in the first place.

### Testing

Three new tests in `tunnelAgentHost.contribution.test.ts`: a max-attempts pause resuming on focus (with the rate limit still suppressing repeats), a confirmed-online status check resuming a max-attempts pause, and `clearConnection()` firing only on a connected → disconnected transition. Each was verified to fail without the corresponding fix.

title: Serve cloud sandbox history when the environment is gone
body:
## The problem

A managed sandbox's compute can be deleted. Once it is, the AHP relay to it is gone for good — and since the relay was the *only* path to a session's history, opening such a session refused to open at all. The user got a session that wouldn't load and no stated reason why.

There was a TODO acknowledging this:

> `// TODO: when the environment is unreachable, render the session's history read-only and queue follow-ups until the host reconnects, as github-ui does. That needs a history source that does not depend on the relay, which we do not have yet.`

## What changed

**1. History that outlives the sandbox.** Mission Control mirrors every `ActionEnvelope` it relays, so the conversation can be rebuilt from `GET /agents/tasks/<id>/events` without the sandbox. New `taskEventReplay.ts` folds those frames back into session and chat state using **the same `sessionReducer` / `chatReducer` the live subscriptions use**, so a replayed session and a live one cannot drift. It only decodes the transport boundary: ordering, chunk reassembly, and the minimal envelope shape.

**2. Rendering no longer waits on `/connect`.** Mission Control blocks on the compute resume before replying, so that call can occupy its entire request budget. Measured on a deleted sandbox: the transcript was ready at 500ms and the session rendered 9.2s later, purely waiting for `/connect` to time out.

The connect and the history fetch now overlap, and whichever lands first decides what the user sees:

| | |
|---|---|
| connect wins | live session, unchanged |
| history wins | session renders (~500ms), connect keeps running |

**3. Read-only is concluded, not assumed.** A session that renders early is *not* marked read-only — `offline` can't distinguish a suspended sandbox that will wake from a deleted one, and presenting the former as read-only would be wrong. `isReadOnly` is an observable, so once the connect actually fails the composer disappears **in place**, without a reopen. If the connect succeeds instead, the stand-in is dropped and the live handler takes over.

**4. `/connect` is no longer retried.** Its answer already reflects the resume it just attempted, so re-asking only repeats the wait. `202 waking` remains the one polled case, against Mission Control's own `Retry-After`.

**5. Rename.** `ICloudSandboxCredentialsService` → `ICloudSandboxApiService`. It now also reads environment and task records, discovers sessions, and replays history — "credentials" stopped describing it. File moved with `git mv` so history follows.

## Notes for reviewers

- **`_activateReadOnly` vs `_settleReadOnly` are deliberately separate.** Registering a content provider no longer implies a verdict about the environment; that split is what lets the optimistic render exist.
- **Two read-only mechanisms exist and only one applies here.** `chatWidget.ts` skips `IChatSession.isReadOnly` when `isSessionsWindow`, so in the Agents window it's the provider-level `setReadOnly` → `interactivity` chain that does the work. `_settleReadOnly` sets both.
- **Provider-level read-only is host-wide**, not per-session — correct for a dead environment, since all of its sessions are equally unreachable.
- **A stand-in registered mid-connect is dropped in `onDidChangeConnections`** before the connection is wired. Registering two content providers for one session type throws, and wiring publishes the session.
- **Divergence from github-ui, on purpose:** its `replayTaskAhpEvents` throws when a task owns more than one session. This one folds each separately, which matters for the proposed fork-sessions design (forked children register under the *source* task). Covered by a test.
- **Truncation is surfaced, not hidden.** A history that ends mid-action returns the complete actions plus `truncated: true`, rather than presenting a partial transcript as whole.

## Known gap

Between render and verdict there's a window (up to the connect budget) where the composer is enabled but no host exists. A message sent in that window has nowhere to go. It only affects dormant environments. If it proves to be a real hazard, the fix is a third "connecting…" state rather than either extreme.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run precommit` (hygiene) ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅
- 39 unit tests passing across `taskEventReplay`, `cloudSandboxAgentHost`, `cloudSandboxCredentialRefresh`, `cloudSandboxTelemetry`

Behavior verified against a real deleted sandbox (`failed to resume agent compute`) by instrumenting the client and reading Mission Control's actual responses.

title: Consolidate chat input notices behind one arbitration host
body:
## The problem

Five surfaces render in the space directly above the chat input:

| Surface | Owner |
|---|---|
| Notifications (quota, promo, permissions, extension API) | `chatInputNotificationWidget.ts` |
| Voice Mode introduction | `voiceModeOnboarding.ts` |
| Dictation introduction | `dictationOnboarding.ts` |
| Getting-started tips | `chatWidget.ts` **and** `newChatWidget.ts` |
| Sub-session "New chat tip" | `newChatInSessionWidget.ts` |

Each time a new one shipped, it bolted its own suppression hack onto the previous, so we ended up with **three overlapping mechanisms** all answering "should the tip be showing?":

1. **CSS** — a `display: none !important` sibling selector in `chatInputNotificationWidget.css`
2. **Boolean flags** — `_isInputOnboardingVisible` / `_isInputNotificationVisible`, duplicated in *both* parent widgets, fed by `onDidChangeInputOnboardingVisible` / `onDidChangeInputNotificationVisible` callbacks plumbed up from the input purely to hide tips
3. **Direct DOM mutation** — `ChatInputOnboarding.setTipsVisible()` reaching across into another widget's tip container and setting its inline style, with `tipContainer` threaded through `registerHost()` into both onboarding services

On top of that, tip rendering was **duplicated** (~165 lines) across the workbench `ChatWidget` and the Agents window `NewChatWidget`, and the two copies had already drifted — the workbench path called `tipPart.domNode.remove()` on hide; the Sessions copy did not.

## The change

One `ChatInputNoticeHost` per input arbitrates precedence with counted claims:

```
Notification  >  Onboarding  >  Tip
```

The rule is a single sentence: **the newest claim in the lowest occupied lane leads; everything else stands down but keeps its claim.** Precedence between categories and recency within a category are the same mechanism.

All three suppression mechanisms are deleted. All five producers — including the sub-session tip, which previously rendered unmanaged DOM — now claim a lane. Tip rendering moves into a single shared `ChatInputTipPresenter` used by both surfaces, with the per-surface differences reduced to one `isEligible` callback.

Displacement is **not** dismissal — a claim is held while hidden, so content returns automatically the moment whatever displaced it goes away.

## Bugs found and fixed

Each of these has a regression test that I verified **fails against the unfixed code**:

- **First-run introductions could be silently spent.** `dispose()` wasn't terminal, so tearing down an input released its notification lease, promoted a pending onboarding claim, and ran `build()` on a dying widget — writing the "seen" storage key for a card the user never saw.
- **A displaced introduction kept the microphone open.** Standing down only hid the DOM; the card stayed alive with its waveform painting and `MicrophonePreview` holding the mic. Added a `setVisible` suspend/resume hook to the banner contract.
- **A card moved between inputs was immediately hidden.** Releasing the claim left behind on the old input reported "stood down" through the same unscoped callback, putting the new card away.
- **A tip could flash in and log a false `shown` telemetry event.** `request()` released its claim before re-claiming, leaving the lane momentarily free.
- **Focus was stranded on `<body>`** when a focused notice was displaced or dismissed — which also drops the context keys the chat keybindings depend on. Now centralized in the host for displacement; producers keep it for user-initiated dismissal.
- **The notice focus command could act on the wrong window.** Host selection didn't check the active document and didn't prefer the focused input.

**"Toggle Focus Between Notice and Input" never worked in the Agents window.** It routed through `IChatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget`, and the Agents composer is not an `IChatWidget`. A small window-level hub resolves the target instead, scoped by a new focus-scoped `ChatContextKeys.inChatComposer` (an earlier revision gated on `IsSessionsWindowContext`, which was window-wide and would have bound the shortcut everywhere in the Agents window).

## On the line count

**+1824 / −428 across 29 files** — of which **+753 is tests**. Production is +1071/−338.

Being straight: this does not reduce total lines. It trades net lines for collapsing three mechanisms into one, deduplicating tip rendering, and fixing the six bugs above. The next surface to appear in this space costs "pick a lane, ~5 lines" instead of "invent a fourth hack and touch two widgets."

The diff was reviewed by six independent critics across three axes (minimality, architecture, over-complexity). Cuts made on their feedback:

- **Deleted `ChatInputNoticeBanner`** — a shared shell with exactly one consumer.
- **Deleted the `UserRequested` lane** and all `isUserRequested` plumbing.
- **Removed the observable/`isSuppressed` mechanism** — the tip presenter both read *and* wrote it, creating a cycle that forced several re-entrancy guards and made the side-effecting `getWelcomeTip()` run twice per render. There is now one protocol.
- **Moved feature wiring out of the primitive** — `chatInputNoticeHost.ts` now imports only `base/common/lifecycle`.
- **Reverted an unrelated `ChatTipService` change** (a location-gate reorder) to its own follow-up; that file is byte-identical to `main`.
- **Trimmed redundant tests** — each cut verified by reverting the production code it claimed to protect and confirming it still passed.

One reviewer-recommended change I **rejected**: converting `occupy()` to a two-phase claim/`activate()` API. It typechecked clean and silently broke 18 tests, because the handle still extended `IDisposable` — forgetting `activate()` is a no-op the compiler can't catch. That exports an ordering obligation to every caller to remove ~18 lines of tested, localized guards.

## Validation

- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check` — clean
- **2838 chat + 1229 sessions tests passing**, 0 failing
- Verified live in a running Code OSS build via Playwright, in **both** the workbench and the Agents window: a notification suppressed the tip, dismissing it restored the tip automatically, and the seam measured 0px gap with squared top corners

## Deliberately not in scope

- **Visual unification.** The five notices still have four rendering paths and four stylesheets, with duplicated container chrome and inconsistent tokens (two use a hardcoded `1px` border where others use `--vscode-strokeThickness`). This PR unifies *behaviour* only. Tracked in #330307 — that work is mostly deletion, and it is much cheaper now that all five producers share one protocol.
- **Tips still don't announce** to screen readers (focus-read `aria-label` only). A live region would make every empty chat speak — a product call.
- **Severity still can't drive lanes.** `"Usage Blocked"` ships as `Info` + `dismissible: true`; a blocking lane needs opt-in metadata, not severity.
- **Tip `shown` telemetry still logs at selection**, not presentation — more correct, but it would shift dashboard numbers.

title: [Agent Host BYOK] Responses reasoning continuation loses its stateful marker
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 x64 (build 26100)
- Feature: Agents window, agent mode
- Selected model: Reasoning-capable extension-contributed BYOK model
- API: OpenAI Responses-compatible

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No. The reproduction requires the built-in Agent Host and an extension-contributed BYOK provider.

## Description

A multi-turn Agent Host BYOK request can lose its `stateful_marker` between the initial response and a tool continuation.

The initial request succeeds and reaches the configured provider. The provider returns a response ID, and the extension emits a `stateful_marker` data part.

During the next continuation attempt:

- The request re-enters the extension with no stateful marker.
- No subsequent outbound provider request is sent.
- Agent Host retries the same deterministic failure five times.
- The final error is:

```text
502 OpenAI Responses reasoning tool continuation is missing its state marker. Start a new chat.
```

The total retry delay was approximately 32 seconds.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an extension-contributed BYOK model backed by an OpenAI Responses-compatible endpoint.
2. Open the Agents window and select the model.
3. Send a request that causes the model to use a tool.
4. Allow the tool result to continue the same turn.
5. Observe the continuation failure and repeated local retries.

## Expected Behavior

The stateful marker should be preserved across the Agent Host bridge and supplied to the next reasoning or tool continuation.

If the marker cannot be preserved, the request should fail once with a clear diagnostic instead of retrying the same deterministic failure.

## Actual Behavior

The initial request succeeds and emits a stateful marker. The marker is absent when the continuation re-enters the extension, and the Agent Host retries the failure five times.

## Additional Context

This appears specific to the Agent Host BYOK Responses path. The observed request sequence places the loss after the extension emits the marker and before the next provider request.

Related implementation work: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328146

title: editor: don't reindent the line following a pasted block (real-world bug)
body: Hi! This fixes a long-standing paste bug: when you paste a block of code, the line *after* the pasted text gets reindented, even though it wasn't part of the paste. This is a real-world bug, not a synthetic edge case. It's been reported twice by two unrelated people: - #143573 (2022, Ruby) — closed as wont-fix on the assumption that Ruby's indentation rules were at fault - #221574 (2024, PHP) — still open, hit while editing a WordPress theme template Here's the PHP report from #221574. Paste a replacement `` line, and the closing `` below it silently moves one tab to the right: ```html ``` ## Cause It's not language-specific — it reproduces on Ruby, PHP and others. The paste range is built as *pre-paste cursor → post-paste cursor*. So when the pasted text ends with a line break, the range ends at **column 1 of the following line** — a line that received no pasted characters at all. `AutoIndentOnPaste.trigger` then applies its indentation offset to every line up to and including `range.endLineNumber`, which sweeps up that innocent following line. ## Fix Exclude that last line from the reindent when it holds no pasted characters *and* the paste started at the beginning of a line, so the line kept its own indentation intact. The "started at the beginning of a line" part matters: if the paste starts mid-line, the final line of the range is the remainder of the line that got split, which really did lose its leading whitespace and should still be reindented. There's a test covering that. ## Tests Four new tests in `indentation.test.ts`, from the two issues: - `Auto Indent On Paste - Ruby` — the two repros from #143573, plus the mid-line split case - `Auto Indent On Paste - PHP` — the repro from #221574 All four fail before the change and pass after it. The full editor test suite is green (5160 passing). ## Note on #221574 This fixes the first scenario in that issue, but not its headline request. That issue also asks for the pasted block's *relative* indentation to be preserved and the block shifted as a unit, which is a separate gap and still belongs to the tree-sitter indentation work.

title: tunnels: deduplicate dev tunnels and allow managing them
body:
## Problem

`code tunnel` lowercases the machine name when registering a dev tunnel ([`dev_tunnels.rs`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/cli/src/tunnels/dev_tunnels.rs#L827)), but the in-editor "Allow remote session access" path did not. A machine named `Foo-PC` therefore registered as `foo-pc` from the CLI and `Foo-PC` from the editor, leaving two entries for the same machine — and there was no way to clean them up from the UI.

The naming logic was duplicated verbatim in `remoteTunnelService.ts` and `tunnelHostMainService.ts`, which is how the two drifted apart.

## Changes

**Consistent naming** — extract the shared `normalizeTunnelName` into `platform/remoteTunnel/common`, matching the CLI (lowercase, `[\w-]` only, max 20), and use it from both callers.

**Stop creating duplicates** — `startHosting` now adopts an existing idle launcher tunnel with the same name instead of always creating a new one, and only deletes tunnels it created, so a tunnel the CLI persisted is left intact. Adoption is skipped entirely when the tunnel already has the right labels and agent host port (the common case makes zero mutating calls), and falls back to creating a tunnel if the service rejects any part of the reconciliation.

**Delete tunnels** — each entry in the dev tunnel picker gets a delete button with a confirmation. The description now shows whether the tunnel is online rather than its protocol version.

**Rename tunnels** — a `Remote Connections: Rename Tunnel` command, linked from the "Allow remote session access" hover, sets the tunnel name without having to hunt down `remote.tunnels.access.hostNameOverride`. Validation matches the CLI's `is_valid_name`.

## Notes for reviewers

Adopting an existing tunnel has to respect several dev tunnels service rules that only surface against the live service — ports cannot be sent on an update, an existing port's protocol cannot be changed (the CLI registers this port as `auto`, we create it as `https`), and the SDK mutates the request-options object it is handed, so each call gets its own. The steady-state path avoids all of it by not writing at all.

Verified with `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, and the tunnel unit tests. The adoption path is not reachable from the test suite — it only exercises against the live dev tunnels service — so it is worth a smoke test on a machine that already has a `code tunnel` registered. The "Remote Connections" output channel logs which path was taken.

Fixes #329063

title: Offload large Copilot CLI tool results to disk above 8KB
body:
Agent Host Copilot CLI sessions inherited the runtime's default 20KB large-output threshold. This lowers it to 8KB — the same threshold the Copilot extension uses for `chat.agent.largeToolResultsToDisk.thresholdBytes` — so verbose tool results are written to a temp file and replaced with a path + preview instead of consuming the context window.

### What changed

`CopilotSessionLauncher._buildSessionConfig` now sets the SDK's `largeOutput` session option:

```ts
largeOutput: {
    maxSizeBytes: 8 * 1024,
},
```

Because this lives in the shared config builder, it applies to every launch route: `createSession`, `resumeSession`, the custom-agent resume retry, and the empty-session fallback create.


### Known follow-up (not addressed here)

The runtime's `view` tool description and Claude exploration instructions statically say files truncate at 20KB, but the configured session threshold is what `view` actually enforces. With this change a 12KB file is documented as readable yet returns large-file guidance. That is a runtime-side wording issue tracked separately; it does not affect the generic tool-result offload message, which reports the real size.
